run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T09:12:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: RequestErrorRate is firing for otel-demo/frontend-proxy because that service's `ingress` server spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR continuously, not because of a pod outage. The proxy's own access log shows the concrete failures: sporadic `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` responses (upstream response time ~200-900 ms) against the `frontend` upstream, plus an earlier burst of `504 UT response_timeout` (15000-15002 ms) on `GET /api/data` between 08:52:43 and 08:53:06. The sustained trickle (0.0111-0.0333 errors/s against ~7-15 UNSET ingress spans/s; 0.60% of ingress spans over 09:00-09:29) matches the alert's reported value 0.0111 and predates the alert start 09:12:30. A separate ~10x spike (1.03-1.07 errors/s) at 09:16:30-09:17:30 immediately followed a `kubectl rollout restart` of the cart Deployment at 09:15:00 (old pod killed 09:15:03, identical template), and frontend error spans in that window are exclusively cart/checkout operations. All pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts except fraud-detection, which was OOMKilled at 09:20:30 (exit 137) - after the spike and not tied to the proxy's error signals. The failing leg is attributed to the frontend upstream (response flags and `router frontend egress` error spans with http.status_code 0); the mechanism inside the frontend that terminates connections could not be observed because frontend logs, post-~09:00 Jaeger spans and change history are unavailable. Chronic CPU saturation of frontend (0.079-0.114 cores vs 100m limit, 33-43% CFS periods throttled) and frontend-proxy (0.021-0.029 vs 30m limit) is constant across the window and therefore does not explain the onset.

claims.text: frontend-proxy `ingress` spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR throughout the observed window: 0.0111-0.0333 errors/s at 30 s steps from 09:02 to 09:28, against 7-15 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans/s, with a distinct spike to 1.0333-1.0667 errors/s at 09:16:30-09:17:30.

The alert's reported value 0.01111111111111111 matches the sustained low-level error rate of frontend-proxy: the 5-minute error rate was 0.015/s at 09:30 (vs 6.585/s UNSET spans), and the ingress error fraction over 09:00-09:29 was 0.00604 (0.60%) while the 20-minute error increase at 09:29 was 106.86 errors.

The proxy's access log records the concrete 5xx: `504 UT response_timeout` for `GET /api/data` (and /api/data?contextKeys=...) at 15000-15002 ms between 08:52:43 and 08:53:06, and isolated `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` entries at 08:53:32, 08:54:28, 08:54:44, 08:56:00, 08:58:04, 08:59:07, 09:00:20, 09:01:34, 09:03:25 and 09:03:37 on /api/products/*, /api/data*, /api/cart and /api/recommendations, each with upstream response time 200-900 ms and the upstream cluster named `frontend`.

A 503 `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` was also logged at 09:13:17.245 for `GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP` (status 503, upstream response time 658 ms), showing the same response class is present after the alert start, between the 09:03:37 entry and the alert window end.

In the trace sample of error traces (08:52:50-09:00:21), frontend-proxy `ingress` spans fail with http.status_code 504 after 15.00 s and are children of load-generator `GET` spans that also ended 504 after ~15.0 s; the sibling `router frontend egress` spans of the same traces carry error=true with http.status_code 0, i.e. the failing leg is the call from the proxy to its frontend upstream.

frontend-proxy has exactly two operations - `ingress` (server) and `router frontend egress` (client) - and only these two carry ERROR spans; the egress errors occur only inside the 09:17:30-09:19:30 spike (0.3444 errors/s) while ingress errors persist at 0.0037-0.0185 errors/s before and after it.

At 09:28 the only services with non-zero error-span rates were frontend-proxy 0.0088/s, ad 0.0018/s, fraud-detection 0.0018/s and recommendation 0.0018/s; frontend, cart, checkout, payment and accounting were 0, and over the whole window frontend's own error spans appear only at 09:17:30-09:19:30 (1.4037 errors/s).

frontend's error spans in the 09:17:30-09:19:30 window are exclusively cart/checkout operations: `GET /api/cart` 0.0852/s, `POST /api/cart` 0.1926/s, `executing api route (pages) /api/cart` 0.2778/s, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` 0.0667/s, `grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem` 0.1926/s, `grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart` 0.0852/s, `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` 0.0667/s and `tcp.connect` 0.0259/s; all other frontend operations were 0.

The cart Deployment was restarted during the window: a new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d was created at 2026-11-16T09:15:00Z carrying annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:15:00Z with the same image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart) and identical env as the old ReplicaSet cart-755465879b (now 0 replicas); events show ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 at 09:15:00, SuccessfulCreate of cart-84889c965d-tkxdz, Killing of cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and SuccessfulDelete at 09:15:03.

frontend p90 span latency was 174-204 ms from 08:55 to 09:15, rose to 233/299/303 ms at 09:17:30-09:21:30 and returned to 160-178 ms by 09:27; frontend p99 was 669-800 ms except 1246-1288 ms in the same spike, and no individual frontend operation exceeded p99 1332 ms at 09:28. No sustained latency increase accompanies the persistent error trickle.

frontend runs at its CPU limit: 0.079-0.114 cores used against a 100m limit with 33.6-43.2% of CFS periods throttled steadily across the whole window; frontend-proxy uses 0.0215-0.0293 cores against a 30m limit with 7.3-12.1% throttled periods. Neither value changes at the alert start.

frontend and frontend-proxy pods are the only endpoints of their Services (frontend -> pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8, frontend-proxy -> pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt), both pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, and all five nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False.

Neither the frontend nor the frontend-proxy Deployment defines a readiness probe, and their container limits are 100m/200Mi (frontend) and 30m/50Mi (frontend-proxy); all 21 otel-demo Deployments report spec.replicas 1 and readyReplicas 1.

fraud-detection's container was OOMKilled at 09:20:30 (exitCode 137, reason OOMKilled) and restarted at 09:20:31 with restartCount 1; its working set had climbed 350 MB -> 416 MB before that against a 400Mi limit and later read 595 MB and 788 MB at 09:22:30/09:24:30 before falling to ~398 MB.

ad's latency and error signals are not degraded while the alert persists: ad p90 dropped from 124.99 ms at 08:55:30 to 2.85-3.83 ms from 09:23 to 09:29, its `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean` error rate was 0 across the series and its `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` error series was 0 except three isolated 0.0037/s blips.

In the 08:52-09:00 trace sample, ad's `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean` spans carry error=true with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and durations 1.1-6.5 s in the same traces that contain the frontend-proxy 15 s /api/data 504s.

The flagd ConfigMap `flagd-config` currently sets `cartFailure` to defaultVariant `on` while every other flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) defaults to `off`. The cart service's own span metrics show no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for its operations (GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart spans are all UNSET) at a steady 5-6 spans/s.

The only ERROR-class span metrics available for this target are `traces_span_metrics_calls_total` and `traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket`; no `rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*`, `http_server_request_duration_*` or `app_payment_transactions_*` series were returned for the window, so error codes and upstream status could only be read from trace spans and the Envoy access log.

The sustained alert is driven by the frontend (Deployment frontend) terminating in-flight upstream connections: the proxy answers 503 with response flag `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against the `frontend` upstream roughly every 30-90 s, which keeps the error rate at 0.0111-0.0333/s. What makes the frontend close those connections (e.g. server-side keep-alive/abort behaviour under its chronically saturated CPU) cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.

The 09:16:30-09:17:30 error spike (ingress 1.03-1.07 errors/s, frontend 1.40 errors/s) was a transient consequence of the cart Deployment restart at 09:15:00: killing cart-755465879b-rh5r4 broke the frontend's in-flight cart gRPC calls, and the frontend's only error spans in the window are CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and /api/cart routes; the rate fell back to the 0.011/s baseline by 09:19:30.

The 08:52:43-08:53:06 burst of 15 s `504 UT response_timeout` on `GET /api/data` (the frontend route that evaluates feature flags) was caused by the flagd dependency becoming slow/unresponsive at that time, as suggested by ad's flagd `ResolveBoolean` DEADLINE_EXCEEDED spans of 1.1-6.5 s in the same traces and ad's p90 of 125 ms at 08:55:30 that later fell to ~3 ms; no flagd logs or flagd error spans were retrievable to confirm it.

Chronic CPU saturation contributes to the frontend's long tail (p99 669-800 ms) and to occasional aborted/slow responses: frontend consumes its entire 100m limit (0.079-0.114 cores) with 33-43% of CFS periods throttled and frontend-proxy consumes 0.0215-0.0293 of its 30m limit with 7-12% throttled. Because both ratios are flat from 08:55 to 09:29, this is a standing condition rather than the trigger of the alert.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKill caused this alert. fraud-detection was OOMKilled at 09:20:30, after the alert start (09:12:30) and after the 09:16:30-09:17:30 proxy spike; frontend-proxy ingress errors were already 0.0111-0.0185 errors/s at 09:02-09:12, and frontend's error spans never involve fraud-detection operations, so its restart explains its own error blips but not the proxy's sustained rate.

Rejected as the origin of the alert: the cart Deployment restart is not what started it. The proxy's ingress error rate was already non-zero (0.0111-0.0222/s) at 09:02-09:12, before the 09:15:00 rollout restart, and the restart's pod template is identical (same image and env), so it is a deliberate rollout that transiently amplified the rate rather than the cause of the sustained condition.

The frontend's own signals do not show a hard failure during the sustained trickle: the pod is Ready with 0 restarts, produces no error spans between 09:19:30 and 09:29, and its p99 latency stays at 669-800 ms, so the evidence that connections were terminated comes only from the proxy's access log and its `router frontend egress` error spans, not from a frontend-side error signal.

The blast radius is narrow: the ingress error fraction over 09:00-09:29 was 0.60%, only 0.0088-0.015 error spans/s at 09:28-09:30, and no other otel-demo service showed an error rate above 0.0018/s; the alert condition is therefore satisfied by a very small number of failed requests rather than a broad outage.

Collect the frontend application logs and its HTTP server keep-alive/abort configuration (the frontend container emitted no readable log lines for 09:20-09:26 and its Deployment env sets no such timeouts), and compare the frontend's connection-close behaviour against Envoy's upstream connection reuse, since the 503 UC class is the dominant contributor to the persistent rate.

Raise the frontend container CPU limit above its current 100m (observed usage 0.079-0.114 cores with 33-43% of CFS periods throttled) so its tail latency is not governed by throttling, and review why frontend-proxy (limit 30m, usage 0.0215-0.0293 cores, 7-12% throttled) also sits at its ceiling.

Confirm whether the flagd `cartFailure` flag (currently defaultVariant `on` while all other flags are `off`) is intended, and correlate its change time with the error timeline; this requires the missing change-history integration, since the ConfigMap cannot show when the value changed.

gaps: Jaeger holds no frontend-proxy spans after ~09:00-09:10: traces_search for frontend-proxy over 09:10:00-09:33:42 and traces_search_by_tags error=true over 09:20:00-09:33:42 both returned no data, and the error-trace sample ended at source_end_at 09:00:21, so the sustained 503s cannot be examined per trace.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 09:22:00-09:26:00 (0 bytes read, no_data view), so the frontend-side reason for the connection terminations is unobserved.
frontend-proxy logs are readable only up to 09:25:43.281607Z; a filtered read of 09:24:00-09:25:40 matched no 5xx line (no_data view), and 09:26:00-09:28:00 returned no bytes at all.
list_prometheus_rules returned nothing for RequestErrorRate, so the alert's exact expression, threshold ("above 0") and evaluation window could not be verified against the metric it uses.

The change_history integration is not available, so when the flagd `cartFailure` flag was set to `on` and who issued the 09:15:00 `kubectl rollout restart` of the cart Deployment could not be established.
flagd logs returned no data for 08:45-09:33, so flagd's state during the 08:52-08:56 /api/data timeouts could not be inspected.
No Ingress objects were returned for namespace otel-demo (query returned 0 matches with a no_data status), so upstream ingress-layer causes could not be assessed.

No `envoy_*` metrics and no `rpc_client_duration_*`/`http_server_request_duration_*` series exist on this target, so per-upstream status codes, retry counts and Envoy connection-pool statistics are unknown.
Whether the 503 UC errors also occur in the unread 09:25:43-09:33:42 slice of proxy logs, and their exact per-route distribution after 09:13:17, is unknown.
next_steps: Read the frontend container's stdout/stderr once log retention allows, looking for socket resets, request aborts or keep-alive timeout messages near the 503 timestamps.
Inspect the Envoy bootstrap/route configuration used by frontend-proxy (upstream connection-pool idle timeout, retry policy, 15 s route timeout) against the frontend's server keep-alive settings.

Confirm with the team whether the 09:15:00 cart Deployment rollout restart and the current `cartFailure=on` flagd setting were intentional, using source-control or change-history records that are not integrated in this run.
Track the frontend-proxy ingress error ratio and the 503 UC log count over a longer multi-hour window to distinguish a chronic low-rate condition from a regression at the alert start.
